claims.text: Replacing conventional high-thermal-load laser processing with femtosecond laser powder bed fusion will reduce residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Femtosecond laser powder bed fusion will produce a refined microstructure in AlCrFeNiSi components.
The refined microstructure will improve the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi components.
Pulse energies near the ablation threshold will minimize melt-pool size and thermal input.
The proposed process uses miniature geometries with a thickness of approximately 2 mm in a controlled inert atmosphere.
The proposed processing window includes approximately 100 fs pulses, an adjustable repetition rate around 1 kHz, and low overall energy density.
Femtosecond processing will significantly reduce melt-pool dimensions.
Reduced melt-pool dimensions and lower thermal gradients will minimize grain growth.
Reduced melt-pool dimensions and lower thermal gradients will suppress residual-stress buildup.
Ultrashort pulses deposit energy over extremely short timescales, causing rapid localized melting and ultra-rapid solidification.
Ultrashort-pulse energy deposition minimizes heat diffusion and reduces thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients limit residual-stress formation.
Rapid cooling produces a refined microstructure that enhances both yield strength and ductility relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Femtosecond-processed parts will have a finer and more uniform grain structure than conventionally processed parts.
Femtosecond-processed parts will exhibit higher hardness and strength with reduced embrittlement.
Conventional high-thermal-input additive manufacturing typically produces pronounced thermal gradients, residual stresses, and degraded mechanical properties due to prolonged melt-pool heating.
The intervention is expected to apply primarily to miniature components within a processing window requiring precise control of pulse energy and scan speed.
Scalability to larger geometries or materials with markedly different thermal properties is uncertain.
